subject: Glomex - EU private deploy: egress policy & keystore operator questions
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@glomex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T08:22:00Z
Subject: EU private deploy - question on egress and keystore operator

Rafael —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security team as we move to evaluate Redwood for our EU-only pilot: quick, specific asks so we can close the control gate.

1) Egress controls: if we deploy in Redwood Private (VPC peering + private control plane) and select the EU hosting option, can you confirm that data (request/response payloads, logs, caches) will not traverse non-EU public egress points under normal operation? If there are any control-plane callbacks to Redwood-hosted services, where do those endpoints live?

2) Keystore / KMS operator: for a private deployment do we manage KMS keys (customer-managed), or does Redwood retain operational key access? If Redwood operators ever need to rotate or rekey, what is the approval/rotation workflow and is there an operator roster we can vet?

3) Logging and audit exports: can audit/log exports (access logs, request traces) be kept inside our VPC/region and exported to our SIEM without leaving the EU?

If you can provide short, authoritative answers and any supporting artifacts (SOC2 artifact IDs, SIG/CAIQ pointers, or a short runbook/diagram) we can share with our InfoSec reviewer.

Appreciate it — happy to set a call if helpful.

–Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Security Operations, Glomex
Alex.Mercer@glomex.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@glomex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU private deploy - question on egress and keystore operator

Alex —

Thanks — good, precise questions. High-level answers below; Irene and Ben are cc'd for the technical specifics and operator matrix. Ive attached a short runbook (residency-runbook-Glomex.pdf) that summarizes the flow.

- Egress controls: For a Private deployment in the EU region (customer VPC + private control plane), data paths for inference requests, KV/prefix caches, and logs are confined to the EU zone. Redwood control-plane telemetry that is not required for request routing (health metrics, aggregated billing) can be configured to remain in-region for EU customers; by default we route those endpoints to our EU control-plane endpoints when the deployment is EU-scoped.

- Keystore / KMS operator: In Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) integrated via customer KMS endpoints. When customers opt for BYOK, Redwood holds no plaintext key material. We also offer an optional Redwood-managed HSM-backed KMS for customers that prefer us to manage keys; in that model, operator interventions are rare and documented — Ben will share the operator roster and the rekey workflow.

- Logs & audit exports: Audit logs for Private deployments can be configured to stream to your SIEM over private peering (no public egress). We support S3-compatible endpoints inside the EU region or direct SIEM forwarding via private connectivity.

Next steps: Ben, can you attach the operator matrix and confirm the step-by-step rekey/approval flow? Irene, could you add a short note about control-plane endpoint FQDNs for EU-only customers?

If helpful we can propose an hour on Monday to walk your InfoSec through the artifacts.

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our InfoSec review:

- Can you explicitly list the control-plane FQDNs (or IP ranges) that will be contacted for EU-only deployments? We need to validate firewall whitelists.

- For the BYOK model, can you confirm whether Redwood ever performs any operator-initiated key exports or backups that could be stored off-region? We need an explicit non-export guarantee for our pilot.

If those answers are written up we can move to an NDA and a short tech call.

–Alex

Alex —

Adding the technical specifics below and attaching the peering diagram (privatelink-peering-diagram.png).

1) Control-plane endpoints (EU-only):
- api.eu.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS, 443) — control-plane API for EU customer accounts
- telemetry.eu.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS, 443) — optional (disabled by default) aggregated metrics/usage; can be configured to point to your collector or disabled
- ops-agg.eu.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS, 443) — internal ops aggregation endpoint; for Private deployments it remains in the EU zone and is only reachable over configured private peering.

We will provide the CIDR blocks used for private peering during onboarding (these are stable for the EU region). Whitelisting those CIDRs + the three FQDNs above is sufficient for normal operation.

2) BYOK / key export policy:
- When customers choose BYOK we only store a reference to key material (key ID). We do not import or export plaintext keys. Any backups are encrypted by the customer-managed KMS and never stored in plaintext at Redwood.
- Operator-initiated exports of key material are explicitly disallowed by policy; any exception requires a documented escalation and written customer approval. We can add a contractual clause for Glomex to that effect.

3) Audit logs and trace IDs:
- Yes — per-request correlation IDs (trace_id) are emitted and included in audit records. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via private peering; each log line includes request timestamps, model id, tenant id (masked as requested), and trace_id.

Attachments included: kms-operator-matrix.csv (operator roles + PAM controls), privatelink-peering-diagram.png, residency-runbook-Glomex.pdf.

If this looks good we can produce a one-page statement of EU residency guarantees and fold the rekey/operator clauses into the contract appendix. Rafael — I'll sync with Legal if they want the explicit non-export clause in the MSA.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Head, Residency & Ops Assurance — Redwood Inference
